result.reason: Both replicas identify the same core causal delta: the atmospheric Newcomen cylinder's alternating heat/cool thermal cycle bloated coal consumption and confined engines to coalfield pumping (before-blocker), and Watt's separate condenser removed condensation from the hot cylinder, lowering fuel consumption (basis change, with the sourced 'roughly two-thirds' reduction and 1769 patent framing) and opening a path toward rotative factory power only after later commercialization and mechanical complements (Boulton capital, bored cylinders, rotary transmission, skilled installation, fuel-savings contracts). Differences are only in detail/emphasis and phrasing: A lists the complements inside pathDelta/remainingBoundary while B lists them inside basisChange; A frames the pre-condenser world as lacking a basis for broad rotary power, B frames the later factory-prime-mover path as blocked by the same thermal defect. These are compatible scopes, not incompatible causal stories. Both correctly restrict the evidence ceiling to the single sourced quantitative claim and refrain from unsupported ordering, ranking, diffusion rates, or invention of facts, and both stay within the source's material facts. No material contradiction exists.

Both extractions describe the same causal-delta: Cayley's conceptual decomposition of the fixed-wing aircraft problem into lift/propulsion/control (by 1799) plus glider demonstration (1804) opened a tractable path for solving lift independently while propulsion/control remained open. Before-blocker in both is the undifferentiated conflation of these functions. PathDelta in both is the newly tractable glider/lift sub-path vs. remaining propulsion gap. RemainingBoundary in both is that engines/materials/control for powered flight were still missing. Evidence ceilings are scope-equivalent (thin summary; no design specifics, no downstream influence, no quantitative content). The only material difference is B's addition of 'control' alongside 'lift' in the 1804 glider and the 'century' vs. vague duration phrase, neither of which is load-bearing or contradicts. Both remain source-grounded, never inventing design mechanisms or quantitative/magnitude claims beyond the source.

Both extractions identify the same core causal delta: the Bunsen-Kirchhoff spectroscope (c.1859-60) converted light into a repeatable characteristic line-pattern representation, enabling new-element discovery (cesium/rubidium) and remote celestial composition inference, with the prior blocker being subjective flame color and lack of a general line-to-element/composition link. Path deltas agree (newly open: element discovery via spectra, remote composition without sampling, shared cross-laboratory standard; wet chemistry not closed). Remaining boundaries agree (calibration/reference data still needed; wet chemistry not obsolete). Evidence ceilings agree (no quantitative diffusion, no support for later atomic physics/astrophysics beyond stated second-order). Differences are stylistic paraphrases, such as A's 'cannot support full causal role in later fields' vs B's 'cannot attribute causal priority,' and A's focus on low-concentration vs B's framing of direct sampling, which are semantically equivalent limitations. No material contradiction in load-bearing causal story.

Both extractions interpret the same source-native trajectory—Great Eastern's extreme-scale engineering, unsustainable passenger/commercial model, and later cable-laying role—within the same scope. Each field draws materially equivalent conclusions: basisChange is undeterminable but notes the use-case shift; beforeBlocker is unidentifiable due to lack of a specific blocking relation; evidenceCeiling restricts the source to a descriptive sequence with no causal attribution; pathDelta both identify the commercial path underperforming and the cable-laying role opening; remainingBoundary both disclaim mechanism, timing, actors, and technical specifics. The small wording differences (A calls pathDelta merely 'descriptive observation,' B explicitly says a path 'newly open') describe the same factual transition and are not incompatible load-bearing causal stories. Neither replica invents material facts beyond the source. No material contradiction exists.

Both extractions describe the same underlying causal-delta structure: a serendipitous penetrating-radiation anomaly (noticed outside the expected cathode-ray path, confirmed by varying shielding/absorbers and photographic shadows) opened a new sensing channel whose imaging utility outran settled physical ontology. Both identify the before-state as an ontology/planned-question frame in which hidden internal structure and a separable radiation agent had no causal standing, blocking later paths until the anomaly was probed. Path deltas agree on opening: medical/fracture imaging from early 1896, tracing radiation with screens/plates/absorbers, hazard/safety and eventual dosimetry/protection-organization paths; closing the planned-question-only and ontology-first accounts; and moving safety to an explicit institutional objective (1913 recommendations). Remaining boundaries agree that X-ray physical nature, standardized dose, dose-response quantification, and comprehensive regulation did not follow from discovery or rapid adoption. Evidence ceilings both correctly flag absence of quantitative dose-effect, exact diffusion counts, injury-causation demonstration, and fine-grained timelines. Material facts are faithful to the source (Röntgen, November 1895, fluorescent screen, photographic shadows, skeletal hand, January 1896 fractures, burns/dermatitis/hair loss, 1913 German Roentgen Society). No load-bearing causal incompatibility; differences are wording, elaboration, and added framing (e.g., B's mention of probability/retroactive-invalidation ceilings) rather than contradicting facts.

Both extractions identify the same causal story: break-bulk's repeated manual handling as the blocking condition that a mere box could not overcome absent convergence of interoperable dimensions/corner fittings/procedures (ISO TC104 standards published 1960s), high-capacity cranes, and purpose-built ships/terminals. Both attribute the basis change to standardization plus complementary infrastructure raising crane productivity and enabling reuse across modes, ending proprietary lock-in. Both mark the same path delta (standardized intermodal container system opening, proprietary carrier-specific sizes closed as rival/failure path) and the same remaining boundary (work relocated not eliminated; labor displacement and later environmental/security consequences unresolved). Evidence-ceiling characterizations agree on what the packet supports versus cannot support, differing only in illustrative detail. No load-bearing causal facts are asserted by one and denied by the other, so there is no material contradiction.

Both extractions trace the same causal story: Codd's 1970 relational/data-independence formalization plus System R prototype, SQL set-oriented querying, and cost-based optimization jointly enabled a declarative representation to become practical only when co-produced hidden physical machinery (indexes, optimizer, transactions/recovery, storage) honored it at acceptable cost. The before-blocker fields both identify dependence on physical record navigation, specialist programs, and performance uncertainty as the pre-existing constraint. Path-delta fields both identify the newly opened route from logical specification to optimized physical execution with displacement (not elimination) of hand-crafted navigation and a shift of optimization burden to hidden machinery. Remaining-boundary fields both note diffusion lag, retained physical layout/indexes/cost estimation, and rational early skepticism. Evidence-ceiling fields both flag the co-production thesis as the strongest supported claim and disclaim quantified adoption/parity/harm/institutional evidence. Differences are only in wording and level of detail, not in load-bearing causal content; neither output invents facts beyond the source packet.

Both replicas identify the same causal delta: NCP (single-network host protocol) being insufficient for internetworking, displaced by an end-to-end internetwork protocol architecture where IP datagram delivery is separated from end-to-end transport (TCP), operationalized via BSD distribution and the 1 January 1983 NCP-to-TCP/IP conversion. beforeBlocker, basisChange, pathDelta, and remainingBoundary all describe materially identical relations: the pre-existing single-network NCP limitation; the opening of cross-network routing plus IP/transport separation; the closing of single-network and universal-network/gateway alternatives; and the boundary that nominal protocol breakthrough did not equal broad diffusion, which depended on complements, cost/standards/institutions and the OSI lesson. Both are source-grounded, drawing only on the trajectory's stated observations, rivals, complements, diffusion, and second-order effects; neither invents quantification, adoption rates, lifecycle harms/authority changes, or singular credit. Differences are only in level of detail and phrasing, not incompatible load-bearing causal stories, so there is no material contradiction.

Before-field state (repeated near-misses, no prior target gain), pathDelta (opening repeatable lab ignition/gain as a demonstrable regime), remainingBoundary (gain does not imply energy-system realization per title's 'realization gap'), and evidenceCeiling (single thin summary supporting only the stated numbers and dates, not grid/economics/engineering claims) all match in material scope. Differences are only in phrasing/elaboration (e.g., A computes ratio 1.54, B says output > input; B slightly expands pathDelta framing), none of which constitutes incompatible or invented load-bearing facts. Both stay within source evidence and do not lift the trajectory beyond it.
